relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - incompatibleWithFeature. Distinct from incompatibleWithAccessSurface/incompatibleWithCredentialType (data-plane statement gates); this is a network-connectivity-type feature exclusion. Azure Private Link flatly cannot support XDCR/Prometheus, unlike AWS/GCP Private Link where these same features are supported-with-restrictions (see add-aws-private-link.json, add-gcp-private-link.json).
relations.evidence: Azure Private Link connections do not support [cross data center replication (XDCR)](../clusters/xdcr/xdcr.md) or [Prometheus metrics](../clusters/monitoring/prometheus.md). If you require XDCR or Prometheus metrics, use [VPC Peering](../clouds/private-network.md).

notable_absence.finding: No data-plane privilege/RBAC content - only a management-plane role gate and a support-plan gate, consistent with the rest of this batch's private-link pages.

cross_component_finding: This page's support-plan wording ('Enterprise Support Plan') matches the already-known variant from cloud/security/auditing.json exactly - a genuine recurrence, not a new issue. But its two sibling pages in this SAME batch (add-aws-private-link.md, add-gcp-private-link.md) instead say just 'Enterprise plan', and cmek.md (also this batch) says 'Enterprise plan' too. So within a single 4-page cluster of closely related pages, 2 wordings appear split 3-to-1. This sharpens the existing docs-issue: the inconsistency isn't scattered across unrelated pages, it recurs even among near-identical sibling pages authored for the same feature family.
cross_product_finding: Unlike AWS and GCP Private Link (which support XDCR/Prometheus 'upon request, subject to specific conditions'), Azure Private Link flatly excludes both features and directs users to VPC Peering instead - a genuine per-cloud-provider capability difference within the same Capella feature, not a documentation gap.
